steps.message:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Monokpo-street, Bori Metropolis. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 1426 | 2.2 | 2.2
2 | 569 | 0.998 | 3.2
3 | 1241 | 23.2 | 26.4
4 | 1931 | 30.1 | 56.5
5 | 2994 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as Q-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station Monokpo-street, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Report – Monokpo-street, Bori Metropolis**

The interpreted VES model shows five layers with resistivities of 1426, 569, 1241, 1931, and 2994 ohm-m at increasing depth. The sequence begins with a resistivity drop from Layer 1 to Layer 2 (1426 → 569 ohm-m), followed by a consistent increase through Layers 3, 4, and 5 (569 → 1241 → 1931 → 2994 ohm-m).

Applying standard curve-type notation: Layers 1-2-3 give H (r1 > r2 < r3), Layers 2-3-4 give A (r2 < r3 < r4), and Layers 3-4-5 give A (r3 < r4 < r5). This yields a curve type of **HAA**, not a pure Q-type (which would require continuously decreasing resistivity with depth). The on-file Q-type label does not match the computed layer sequence and should be corrected to HAA for accurate hydrogeological interpretation at this station.
